name: The Jesus Lizard
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two Scratch Acid refugees moved to Chicago, found a guitarist and a drummer, and made four records with Steve Albini. Then came Capitol, a split, and Rack, 26 years after the last album.

eras.title: From Austin to Humboldt Park
eras.text: Scratch Acid had just broken up in Austin when guitarist Duane Denison asked David Yow to play on some recordings; Yow offered to sing instead and brought bassist David Wm. Sims. By 1989 all of them were in Chicago, sharing one apartment, recording with Steve Albini and signed to Touch and Go.

years.h: Denison asks for a player and gets a singer
years.p: Denison asks ex-[[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]] frontman Yow to join some sessions; Yow counters that he'll sing, with Sims on bass. The name comes from the basilisk, the lizard that runs across water.

years.h: Yow and Sims move to Chicago
years.p: Sims is already in Chicago playing bass in [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]] with Albini and [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]]. Denison follows in 1989.

years.h: The drum machine gets one record
years.p: Recorded with Albini in December 1988 and January 1989, Pure is the band's only record with a machine on drums. That's Sims singing Blockbuster, later covered by [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]].
years.xp: The EP was cut at two Chicago-area rooms, Kitty Empire and Studio Media, and runs 14 minutes and 19 seconds. Sims drew the cover as well as singing Blockbuster; the last track is titled Happy Bunny Goes Fluff-Fluff Along.

years.src: Vice: The Jesus Lizard Book · setlist.fm
years.h: The first show is at a Thai restaurant
years.p: With [[Mac McNeilly|3ba1e445-feaf-4713-ba50-ff077fffd544]], ex-Phantom 309, replacing the drum machine, the band debuts at Bangkok Bangkok in Chicago on a bill with [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] and King Kong.
years.xp: Yow told Vice the diners' tables faced away from the stage and food kept coming out through the set. His own stagecraft that night: "I had my hands in my pockets the whole time. I was terrified."

years.h: Four men, three bedrooms, 2722 W. Potomac
years.p: All four members move into one apartment in Humboldt Park at $625 a month. They stay long enough to see the rent climb to $675.
years.xp:
The band described the block to the Chicago Reader as a drive-through drug zone with competing gangs. Day jobs: Sims at a record distributor in Des Plaines, Denison at Foodworks and giving guitar lessons, McNeilly stuffing records into sleeves at Touch and Go.

Denison told Guitar World the four were around each other 24-7, and that arguments ran to "punches, shoving. Lamps and other objects thrown." Home shows were at Metro, $8 to $10 a ticket.

eras.title: Albini's best band of the '90s
eras.text: Albini recorded four straight albums and kept Yow's voice down in the mix with the instruments. The records are exact and mean; the shows were the opposite, with Yow out on the crowd and often out of his clothes.

years.h: Head, and a drummer compared to Charlie Watts
years.p: Twenty-seven minutes on Touch and Go. Trouser Press compared McNeilly's poker face behind the kit to Charlie Watts.
years.xp: Yow recorded his vocal for Pastoral so drunk that, by his account in Louder's album ranking, he had no memory of the session afterward. The CD edition tacks the Pure EP on the end.

years.src: Vice: The Jesus Lizard Book · Wikipedia: The Jesus Lizard
years.h: Most nights, Yow sings from on top of the audience
years.p: Yow sings from on top of the audience and strips, licks and climbs on people. Michael Azerrad said he sounded like a kidnap victim howling through duct tape.
years.xp:
The song Tight 'n Shiny began as an instrumental called Metropolis. Yow says he started exposing himself during it because "I didn't know what else to do!" Albini called it the funniest thing he'd ever seen.

The bills came due. In Zurich the crowd passed an unconscious Yow back onto the stage and he told the paramedics "Nicht ist los." In Albuquerque, at 37, he got flipped, landed on his tailbone and the tour was cancelled. One Arizona review of a too-drunk night ended: "David Yow, you owe me twelve dollars."

years.src: Wikipedia: Goat · Vice: The Jesus Lizard Book
years.h: Goat is the one Pitchfork ranks among the '90s' best
years.p: Recorded with Albini at Chicago Recording Company in September 1990. Pitchfork later put Goat at No. 38 on its list of the '90s' best albums.
years.xp: What looks like flames on the cover is a photograph of a topless woman with an image of nails projected on her body, made by Sims. Mouth Breather, Seasick and Then Comes Dudley are here. In Milwaukee Yow once forgot every word of Then Comes Dudley and yelled "Dudley!" for the whole song.

years.h: A painting called Allegory of Death fronts Liar
years.p: Cut in May 1992 at Chicago Recording Company. The cover is Malcolm Bucknall's painting Allegory of Death; AllMusic's Mark Deming called Liar maybe the band's best.

years.src: Wikipedia: Puss · Louder: David Yow · Exclaim!
years.h: Nirvana takes the other side, and the Lizard get a UK hit
years.p: Touch and Go pairs Puss with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s Oh, the Guilt. It's the Lizard's only UK hit and Nirvana's sixth.
years.xp:
Yow said the band had to decide whether they'd look like they were riding Nirvana's coattails, then did it anyway. The two bands shared bills at Maxwell's in Hoboken in 1990, in Denver in 1991 before Nevermind, and at New York's Roseland Ballroom in 1993.

Years later Krist Novoselic asked Yow to front the surviving members at a Seattle event. Yow took three months of vocal lessons, then, as he told Exclaim!, Dave Grohl said he wanted Paul McCartney and Neil Young instead.

yt: Glamorous, as aired on Beavis and Butt-Head
years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head approve of Glamorous
years.p: Two studio tracks, Glamorous and Deaf as a Bat, plus four live ones. The Glamorous video got aired, and approved, on Beavis and Butt-Head.

years.h: A CBGB set becomes a live album on a Warner label
years.p: The band's set at CBGB in New York becomes the live album Show, out in 1994 on Collision Arts and Giant Records, a Warner Bros. subsidiary.

years.h: Down is the last one with Albini
years.p: Bucknall painted the cover, Falling Dog, and asked no pay. Down reached No. 64 on the UK albums chart.
years.xp: Nobody in the room loved it. Albini wrote that no advice seemed welcome and the record struck him as weak by their standards. Sims went further and called Down the worst album the band made, saying the band came in under-prepared.

eras.title: The major-label years
eras.text: The move to Capitol paid better and sold worse. A drummer left for his family, a second one left two years later, and Capitol dropped the band partway through the contract.

q: Had we stayed on Touch and Go, we probably would have broken up sooner.
years.src: Boing Boing · Chicago Reader · The Bad Penny
years.h: The Lizard sign with Capitol Records
years.p: Albini's verdict on the move. McNeilly's version: they wanted an advance and to do responsible things like buy houses.
years.xp:
To Albini, leaving Touch and Go meant abandoning the scene that let them flourish "to become a third-string act for a big corporation that didn't give a shit about them or their audience." He still called them the best band of the '90s, hands down.

Denison, in a 1999 interview, flipped it: Capitol didn't kill the band, and staying independent would have ended it sooner.

years.h: Cincinnati police arrest Yow after his Lollapalooza set
years.p: On a tour with Sonic Youth, Hole, Pavement and Beck, Yow drops his pants at Riverbend Music Center, he said to protest the city's censorship of a Mapplethorpe exhibit. Police arrest him after the set.
years.xp:
He spent about six hours in the drunk tank, though he wasn't drunk, then pleaded guilty to "recklessly and knowingly exposing his private parts": a $327 fine and a one-year ban from Hamilton County.

When officers asked for his signature on the release paperwork, CityBeat reports, he wrote "YOU SUCK! DAVID YOW."

years.h: Shot, Sims's favorite, is made without Albini
years.p: Produced by Garth Richardson, it peaked at No. 28 on Billboard's Heatseekers. Sims calls it the best album he ever played on.
years.xp: Denison agrees with Sims and has the sales problem to go with it. He told Guitar World that half the people who bought Down on Touch and Go didn't buy Shot, "and Shot was a better album."

years.big: "I felt like I had to pick between the band and family."
years.h: McNeilly picks his kids over the road
years.p: Seven-plus months a year on tour wore him down, he told the Chicago Reader. [[Jim Kimball|93ed63b4-5dc3-4f4d-9a74-b891e0354b76]] of [[Mule|84189509-850d-428b-a8f0-1626cb0eabb3]] takes the kit.

years.h: One EP, three producers: Andy Gill, John Cale, Jim O'Rourke
years.p: The self-titled Jesus Lizard EP on Jetset splits its tracks among [[Gang of Four|d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1]]'s [[Andy Gill|eb3f978d-272a-460d-bc3e-a1a82ecb8147]], [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] and [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]].

years.h: Drummer number three comes from the Wesley Willis Fiasco
years.p: Murphy comes over from the [[Wesley Willis Fiasco|fc7242e2-e873-4a99-9654-5cf2caa50870]], the band built around the Chicago street singer.

years.h: After Blue, nothing for 26 years
years.p: The last Capitol album, and the band's last album of any kind for 26 years.

years.h: The last show is in Umeå, Sweden, ten years to the month
years.p: Dropped by Capitol mid-contract, the band plays Umeå Open and announces the split in June. Denison calls it amicable and mutual.
years.xp: That fall Denison told a zine the last show didn't feel solemn or joyous, because nobody was sure it was the last. He also said: "I can't imagine ever doing a reunion tour. We're already as old as most bands are when they do those awful things!"

eras.title: Day jobs and side bands
eras.text: The four scattered to Nashville, Los Angeles, New York and Evanston. It took Mike Patton, the Melvins and a Touch and Go reissue plan to get them back on one stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jesus Lizard · Chicago Reader · Wikipedia: David Yow
years.h: Tomahawk for Denison, tax returns for Sims
years.p: Denison moves to Nashville and co-founds [[Tomahawk|947911f8-60bc-44ab-9782-f97020f15b43]] with Patton. Yow retouches photos in LA and starts acting; Sims does taxes in New York; McNeilly drums in Mouse.
years.xp: Touch and Go put out Bang, a collection of 7-inch sides and rarities, in 2000. Denison also backed Hank Williams III. Yow sang with Qui and later filled in for Flipper, and turned up in films like I Don't Feel at Home in This World Anymore (2017) and Under the Silver Lake (2018).

years.cap: Yow with Scratch Acid at the Showbox, Seattle, 2006
years.h: Yow and Sims bring back Scratch Acid
years.p: With [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] and [[Brett Bradford|70ab1b12-492b-4031-bccd-c7e402d88353]], the Austin band that started it all plays Touch and Go's 25th anniversary festival in Chicago. Yow had started out in Scratch Acid on bass.

q: Fun and money, in that order.
years.src: The Stranger · Chicago Reader · Wikipedia: The Jesus Lizard
years.h: Mike Patton asks, and they say yes
years.p: Patton and the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] ask for the band at their All Tomorrow's Parties in England; Pitchfork Festival and ATP New York follow. Touch and Go reissues the albums on October 6, remastered by Albini and Bob Weston.
years.xp: Yow told The Stranger he hadn't planned to take his shirt off at ATP and had it off seconds into the first song. The 2009 run wrapped on New Year's Eve.

years.h: The Nashville reunion show comes out as Club
years.p: MVD releases the reunion show as a DVD and double LP. The members say this run was probably their last.

years.h: Yow's solo album, 15 years in the making
years.p: Tonight You Look Like a Spider comes out on Joyful Noise, recorded between 1998 and 2007.

years.src: Vice: The Jesus Lizard Book · Boing Boing
years.h: "Why bother?" Yow asks, then designs the book
years.p: Akashic Books, run by [[Girls Against Boys|837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237]]' Johnny Temple, publishes the band's own history. Yow's first reaction to the idea: "Why bother?"
years.xp: Yow agreed on the condition that he design it, which he did with Henry Owings of Chunklet. Albini's contribution is where "the best band of the 90s, hands down" comes from, along with his line about vanity and short-term greed.

eras.title: Twenty-six years between albums
eras.text: The second reunion stuck. After years of touring the old songs, the band wrote by trading files between cities and made its first album since 1998, on Patton's label.

years.h: Houston gets the first show in eight years
years.p: Announced in September, the second reunion starts at a Houston festival alongside Nine Inch Nails and Solange. Riot Fest in Chicago follows in 2018.

years.cap: Albini with Shellac at All Tomorrow's Parties, 2007
years.h: Steve Albini dies at 61
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] dies of a heart attack. He engineered Pure through Down and remastered the Touch and Go albums in 2009.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rack · Exclaim! · Louder: David Yow
years.h: Twenty-six years later, Rack
years.p: Recorded in Nashville in November 2023 with Paul Allen, out on Patton's Ipecac. Pitchfork ranked it No. 17 among 2024's rock albums.
years.xp:
The songs were built by swapping files between cities, which Yow told Louder felt unnatural. Denison's rule for the sessions: "we have to be brutal with quality control."

Yow sang it with technique left over from the Nirvana gig that never happened. Rack scored 84 on Metacritic and reached No. 7 on the UK independent albums chart.
